finding.severity: must fix before executing the original inspection script
finding.trigger: Parser diagnostics can be warnings without being caught by the script's exception handlers.
finding.original_path: ast.parse(source_text, filename=TARGET, mode='exec') without a local warning-to-error filter
finding.supported_source_fact: CPython v3.12.0 Parser/string_parser.c warn_invalid_escape_sequence selects SyntaxWarning for feature_version>=12 and calls PyErr_WarnExplicitObject with the parser filename and original line.
finding.output_path: Lib/warnings.py _formatwarnmsg_impl formats warning text and requests the source line from linecache; ordinary formatting can therefore emit a source literal and initiate a source-line lookup.
finding.closure: The local catch_warnings/simplefilter('error') makes the native _warnings.c error action raise before its warning-display path. The parser may replace this warning exception with SyntaxError; either form reaches an existing handler that omits messages and source text.
finding.nuance: The pure-Python warnings.warn_explicit fallback contains linecache priming before its error branch. This review uses the actual CPython native PyErr_WarnExplicitObject parser route documented in the pinned source; it does not claim every warning producer on every Python implementation has identical internal I/O.
finding.no_target_execution: ast.parse compiles only to an AST via PyCF_ONLY_AST; the inspected module is never imported or evaluated.

exact_script_edits.after:
with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("error")
            module = ast.parse(source_text, filename=TARGET, mode="exec")
